To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytoplasm lipid droplet (PLD) protein perilpin-2 (Pln2) modulates the expression of microbial genes that direct metabolic flux to the production of growth-promoting metabolites.
Plin2 modulates the microbiome function in the intestine in response to a high-fat diet.
Plin2 is a specific host factor that modulates the effects of diet on microbial gene expression profiles in mice, with the greatest impact occurring on HF diets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how host and microbiome metabolism interact to modulate the development and progression of metabolic diseases.
the effects of diet and genetics on the composition and function of the gut microbial community, and the implications of these effects for human health.
the role that the microbiome plays in the development and progression of obesity and metabolic syndrome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
perilipin-1 and perilipin-4 are not involved in the development of the metabolic syndrome, whereas perilipin-3 and perilipin 2 may have a role.
the Plin2-null genotype is a host determinant of diet-induced changes in microbial gene expression profiles, and this effect is more pronounced in the HF diet.
Plin2 is a host determinant of diet-induced changes in microbial function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Plin2 modulates the microbial response to diet, which in turn influences host metabolism.
Plin2 is a specific host determinant that regulates the functional activity of the gut microbiota in response to dietary changes.
Plin2 is a key host determinant of microbiome functional activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Plin2 is a host protein that regulates the metabolic response to diet and the gut microbiota.
the host genotype can modulates microbial function, and that this can be done without impacting the microbial community structure.
Plin2 modulates the microbiome function and that this modulation is independent of the community composition.
